column13: During the third watch an infant nurses and a woman converses with her husband. Both occurring together happens only in the third watch, when everyone awakens at the same time. column15: And after Adam was driven from Eden, the Name Havayah alone is primarily written, like a weaned child seeking food on his own. column11: Bereshit Rabbah 53:11: ‘“Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian, whom she bore to Abraham, playing” (Genesis 21:9). “She said to Abraham: Banish this maidservant and her son, for the son of this maidservant will not inherit with my son, with Isaac” (Genesis 21:10). “Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian” – Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai said: Rabbi Akiva used to say something derogatory regarding this, but I say something complimentary regarding it. Rabbi Akiva expounded: “Sarah saw [the son of Hagar…playing [metzaḥek]]” – metzaḥek is nothing other than sexual immorality, just as it says: “The Hebrew slave whom you brought to us came to me to play with [letzaḥek] me” (Genesis 39:17). It teaches that our matriarch Sarah would see Ishmael force himself on women, trap married women, and violate them.…’ Context and connection to Machshavot Charutz: In Machshavot Charutz 13, Rav Tzadok cites this midrashic exposition (Bereshit Rabbah 53:11) to illuminate his exposition here (“and the Sages expounded in Bereishis Rabbah (53:11): "'Mocking' (metzachek) denotes nothing other than idolatry, sexual immorality, and bloodshed"; and these are three categories of unholy...”), showing how the translated source sheds light on the supernal levels of Thought (Machshavah), the rectification of human desire and intellect, and the inner light of the Oral Torah developed in Machshavot Charutz.
column13: Idolatry is the middle pillar, Tiferet of the husk flowing from Keter, the impulse to mimic divinity, which is idolatry. column11: Shabbat 105b: ‘The Gemara asks: Say that you heard that Rabbi Yehuda rules that one is liable for performing a labor not needed for its own sake in the case of a constructive act; did you hear him deem one liable in the case of a destructive act? column13: And this spirit of folly is anger itself, as stated in Shabbat (105b): "'One who smashes his vessels in his wrath...' Such is the artifice of the Evil Inclination: today it says to him, 'Do this,' and tomorrow, 'Do that,' until it tells him, 'Go worship idols,' and he goes and does so." And the initial step is smashing his utensils in his fury, for in the moment of rage his intellect (Da'at) departs from him, a spirit of folly settles upon him, and he can easily come to commit a practical sin in reality.

column11: Bereshit Rabbah 64:5: ‘“It was when the time he was there was extended, Avimelekh king of the Philistines looked through the window, and behold, he saw Isaac playing with Rebecca his wife” (Genesis 26:8). “It was when the time he was there was extended” – Rabbi Yoḥanan said: A bad dream, a harsh prophecy, and disproportionate mourning are nullified by the passage of extended time. A harsh prophecy, from where is it derived? It is as Israel would say to the prophet: “The days will lengthen, and every vision will be void” (Ezekiel 12:22). column11: Megillah 12b: ‘The verse states: “On the seventh day, when the heart of the king was merry with wine” (Esther 1:10). column15: And the primordial generations from the dawn of creation occupied the status of “the days of youth” for all humanity. column15: Therefore Hashem swore after the Flood: “While the earth remains... cold and heat... shall not cease” — ensuring that such blinding concealment through worldly expansion would never recur, lest man imagine that autonomy exists at the root; for henceforth bounty flows mediated through constriction: cold balancing heat and winter balancing summer.

column11: Shabbat 104a: ‘The children continued:Kuf: Holy [kadosh], referring to God.Reish: A wicked person [rasha]. Why is the kuf facing away from the reish? column11: Shabbat 104a: ‘The Sages said to Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi: Young students came today to the study hall and said things the likes of which were not said even in the days of Joshua bin Nun. column11: Yevamot 63b: ‘And Rava said: Come and see how good a good wife is and how bad a bad wife is. How good is a good wife? As it is written: Whoever finds a wife finds good. column11: Shabbat 10a: ‘Speaking of prayer, the Gemara relates that Rava saw Rav Hamnuna, who was prolonging his prayer.
